prompt.en: How might assemblies like the sabhā and the samiti have limited the power of the rājā? Which modern institutions perform similar functions today? Write about 80 words.

label.en: The rājā was a clan chief who led in war and protected his people

level1.en: What was the rājā's main role in early Vedic times?

clue.en: The rājā functioned primarily as a clan chief who led the group in warfare and protected its members.

level1.en: Which matters did the sabhā and the samiti take up?

clue.en: The sabhā mainly served a judicial function. The samiti focused on policy decisions and political affairs. So these matters did not rest with the rājā alone.

label.en: Parliaments and constitutions bind leaders today

level1.en: What binds and checks heads of government in a modern democracy?

clue.en: In modern democracies, heads of government are bound by constitutions and parliaments, which are representative bodies that check the powers of elected leaders.

text.en: The rājā was mainly a clan chief, who led the group in war and protected its members.
The sabhā heard cases and the samiti focused on policy and political affairs, so these matters did not rest with the rājā alone.
Today, parliaments and constitutions do a similar job: they bind and check the powers of elected leaders.
